Issues.Title: Recognize `abs(…)` and `sign(…)` as math functions in arbitrary values
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`abs(…)` and `sign(…)` are missing from `MATH_FUNCTIONS` in `packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/math-operators.ts`. The list has every other CSS Values 4 math function, and both places that use it skip these two:

- No whitespace is added around operators inside them. A delay that grows from the middle item, `delay-[calc(abs(var(--i)-2)*50ms)]`, generates `calc(abs(var(--i)-2) * 50ms)`. The browser can't read `var(--i)-2` as a subtraction, so every item gets `0s` (instead of `100ms` for `--i: 0`). `w-[abs(20%-100px)]` generates `width: abs(20%-100px)`, which is dropped as invalid.
- `hasMathFn` doesn't see them, so the value is not inferred as a length. `text-[abs(var(--size))]` generates `color: abs(var(--size))` instead of `font-size`, while `text-[clamp(…)]` already generates `font-size`.

This adds both names to the list. I found this while reading `math-operators.ts`, not in a project. Both functions are Baseline 2025 (Chrome 138, Firefox 118, Safari 15.4).

## Test plan

- Added `abs(…)` and `sign(…)` cases, alone and nested in `calc(…)`, to the math operator table in `decode-arbitrary-value.test.ts`, and `text-[abs(var(--size))]` to the existing `text` test in `utilities.test.ts`. All five fail on `main` (e.g. `Received: "abs(20%-100px)"`, and `color: abs(var(--size))` in the snapshot) and pass with this change.
- `npx vitest run packages/tailwindcss`: 45 files, 5405 tests passed.
- Compiled the classes above on `main` and on this branch, and loaded the CSS in Chrome 156. On `main` the delay is `0s` and the `width` is dropped. On this branch the delay is `0.1s`, the width is `20px`, and the font size is `40px` for `--size: -40px`.
- `prettier --check` on the changed files, and `node ./scripts/changelog.mjs check`.

Not run: `cargo test` and the integration tests, since I don't have the Rust toolchain set up here. The change is in the TypeScript core only.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Recognize `abs(…)` and `sign(…)` as math functions in arbitrary values" (#20716)

Issues.Title: Canonicalization: don't treat different `@scope` variants as the same
Issues.Body:
Fixes #20714

## Summary

Since #20369, variants that generate `@scope` rules wrap them in `context` nodes. The canonicalizer computes a variant's signature by printing the `@apply` result with `toCss`, which prints `context` nodes as an empty string. So every `@scope` variant had the signature `.x {}`, the same as a variant that generates nothing, and canonicalization replaced it with whichever of those variants came first (e.g. `[@scope_(.card)]:flex` → `in-blue:flex`, where `in-blue` scopes to `[data-theme='blue']`).

This PR unwraps the `context` nodes before computing the signature, so it includes the `@scope` rule again, as in v4.3.3.

## Test plan

- Added a regression test: `[@scope_(.card)]:flex` stays as is next to an unrelated `@scope` custom variant, and the equivalent arbitrary variant still canonicalizes to that custom variant. The first assertion fails without this PR.
- `vitest run --project tailwindcss` passes.
- In our design system, which has many `@scope` variants, `@scope-has-nested-focus-visible/tab-set-panel:outline` canonicalized to `@scope-not-has-first:outline` before this PR, and stays as is after.

Issues.Title: Preserve declaration sources in JavaScript keyframes
Issues.Body:
## Summary

When a JavaScript config defines keyframes, `@tailwindcss/postcss` emits their declarations without source locations in development. Vite then logs its missing `from` warning.

Preserve each property's source through config merging and CSS-in-JS conversion. If a second config extends an animation, declarations retained from the first config keep their original source file. This also preserves the directory Vite uses to resolve their relative asset URLs.

Related to #20452. Supersedes #20709.

## Test plan

- Added PostCSS regressions for separate configs and for configs in different directories extending the same animation. The latter checks retained declarations, an overridden declaration, added declarations, and fallback value arrays.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --hideSkippedTests` — 5,917 passed, 1 skipped across 84 files.
- After consolidating source recording into config resolution, `pnpm exec vitest run packages/tailwindcss/src/compat packages/@tailwindcss-postcss/src --hideSkippedTests` — 213 passed.
- Verified a Vite 8.2.0 dev transform reproduces the warning before the fix. With the fix, it emits the configured keyframes without the warning and preserves `/asset.svg` when another config extends the animation from a nested directory.
- Prettier checks for changed files, `git diff --check`, and `node scripts/changelog.mjs check` pass.
- TypeScript checks report the same 22 existing diagnostics as the base, with no added diagnostics. Local validation uses the published macOS Oxide 4.3.5 binding. Rust and browser test suites were not run locally.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Preserve declaration sources in JavaScript keyframes" (#20710)

Issues.Title: Preserve source locations for JavaScript keyframes
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Vite's URL rewriter warns when a PostCSS declaration has no source file. In development, `@tailwindcss/postcss` converts Tailwind's AST directly to PostCSS nodes. The keyframes created from JavaScript theme configs lack source locations, so their declarations trigger the warning even when Vite supplied `from` for the input stylesheet.

Keep the source of each keyframe as configs are merged and attach it to the generated rule and its children. This gives PostCSS the source of the `@config` or `@plugin` directive that contributed the keyframe.

Related to [#20452](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/20452). The case reproduced here uses a JavaScript config with `theme.extend.keyframes` and its matching animation utility.

## Test plan

- Confirmed the regression test fails on `main` with missing source files and passes with this change. It covers keyframes from a base config and a separate extension config.
- Ran `pnpm exec vitest run --hideSkippedTests` and `node scripts/changelog.mjs check`.
- Verified a Vite 8.2.0 dev stylesheet transform with `@tailwindcss/postcss` emits the configured keyframes and no longer logs the missing `from` warning.

Issues.Title: fix: accept readonly arrays for build candidates and Scanner sources
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #20706.

`build()` only iterates its candidates, and `Scanner` only reads its sources, but their public types required mutable arrays. Code holding either as a `readonly` array had to copy it into a mutable one first.

- `packages/tailwindcss/src/index.ts`: `build()` now takes `readonly string[]` in both `compile()` and `compileAst()`.
- `crates/node/src/lib.rs`: `ScannerOptions.sources` is generated as `ReadonlyArray<SourceEntry>` via `#[napi(ts_type = ...)]`.
- Added type-level regression tests for both public types.
- Added a changelog entry.

Mutable arrays remain assignable to `readonly` arrays, so this is backwards compatible.

## Test plan

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts` — 268 passed.
- `tsc -p packages/tailwindcss/tsconfig.check.json --noEmit` — clean (package-scoped check).
- `rustfmt --check --edition 2021 crates/node/src/lib.rs` — clean.
- `node ./scripts/changelog.mjs check` — clean.
- Built `@tailwindcss/oxide` and confirmed the generated `crates/node/index.d.ts` now declares `sources?: ReadonlyArray<SourceEntry>`.
- The new type-level tests assign `readonly` arrays to both APIs, so they fail to type-check against the previous mutable signatures and pass with this change.

## Notes

The `#[napi(ts_type = ...)]` attribute only changes the generated TypeScript declaration; the Rust field remains `Option<Vec<SourceEntry>>`, so there is no runtime change.

Issues.Title: @tailwindcss/oxide segfaults when a process holds more than one Scanner (4.3.3, 4.3.5, linux-x64-gnu)
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

`@tailwindcss/oxide` 4.3.5 (also 4.3.3), native `@tailwindcss/oxide-linux-x64-gnu` binding.

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

Seen first with `@tailwindcss/vite` 4.3.3 under Vitest 5. It reproduces with `@tailwindcss/oxide` alone in plain Node; see below.

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

v26.12.0. The crash also happens with other Node 26 builds.

**What browser are you using?**

N/A

**What operating system are you using?**

Arch Linux, x86_64, kernel 7.2, glibc

**Reproduction URL**

Self-contained script below, run against `apps/web` of https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code (commit `7a64505a21e755498e6b85794124f3754265db38`).

**Describe your issue**

When a process creates more than one `Scanner` and calls `scan()` on them, it intermittently dies with SIGSEGV, or sometimes SIGABRT. A single `Scanner` never crashed in 15 runs, even with repeated `scan()` calls. With 3 scanners × 3 rounds, about 1 run in 4 crashes.

```sh
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code.git
git -C t3code sparse-checkout set apps/web
mkdir oxide-repro && cd oxide-repro && npm init -y && npm i @tailwindcss/oxide@4.3.5
cat > scan.cjs <<'JS'
const [base, n, rounds] = process.argv.slice(2);
const { Scanner } = require("@tailwindcss/oxide");
const scanners = Array.from({ length: +n }, () =>
  new Scanner({ sources: [{ base, pattern: "**/*", negated: false }] }));
for (let r = 0; r < +rounds; r++) for (const s of scanners) s.scan();
console.log("ok");
JS
for i in $(seq 1 15); do node scan.cjs ../t3code/apps/web 3 3 >/dev/null 2>&1; echo -n "$? "; done; echo
# typical output: 0 139 0 0 0 139 0 139 0 0 139 0 0 0 0
# with n=1 (one scanner): all 0
```

In real use, `@tailwindcss/vite` creates one scanner per Vite server. A Vitest workspace with several projects that share a Vite config therefore holds several scanners in one process, and the whole test run segfaults.

From core dumps (4.3.3, no symbols available): the faulting thread is a rayon worker inside the oxide binding. Its stack is a deep repeating `join`/bridge recursion that ends in a byte load through an invalid pointer (`movzbl -0x2(%r8,%rbp,1)` with `r8 = 0x3`). A second rayon worker was in the same routine. Other crashes jumped to address `0x0`. That pattern suggests memory corruption rather than a plain panic.

Our workaround is to avoid creating more than one scanner per process: we stopped Vite's `server.warmup` from loading CSS under Vitest.

Issues.Title: `Scanner`'s `sources` and `build`'s `candidates` refuse a readonly array, though each is only read
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4.3.5, and the insiders build of `main` (`0.0.0-insiders.a3cb19c`)

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

None: TypeScript 7.0.2 (`tsc`) type-checking code that calls `@tailwindcss/node` and `@tailwindcss/oxide`

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

v26.12.1

**What browser are you using?**

N/A

**What operating system are you using?**

Windows 11

**Reproduction URL**

https://github.com/YevheniiKotyrlo/tailwindcss-readonly-inputs

**Describe your issue**

`@tailwindcss/oxide` declares `interface ScannerOptions { sources?: Array<SourceEntry> }`, and the objects `compile` from `tailwindcss` and from `@tailwindcss/node` resolve to declare `build(candidates: string[])`. The scanner only reads its sources and `build` only iterates its candidates, but code that holds either as a readonly array can hand it to neither without copying it into a mutable one:

```ts
export const scanned = (sources: readonly SourceEntry[]): readonly string[] => new Scanner({ sources }).scan();

export const builtWithNode = async (css: string, candidates: readonly string[]): Promise<string> => {
  const compiler = await compile(css, { base: process.cwd(), onDependency: () => undefined });
  return compiler.build(candidates);
};
```

1. `git clone https://github.com/YevheniiKotyrlo/tailwindcss-readonly-inputs && cd tailwindcss-readonly-inputs`
2. `npm install`
3. `npm run check`, which type-checks `index.ts` with `strict: true`.

Expected: no errors: `ScannerOptions.sources` takes a `readonly SourceEntry[]` and `build` a `readonly string[]`, while a mutable array still type-checks at both.

Actual, on the insiders build of `main`:

```text
System: MINGW64_NT-10.0-26300, node v26.12.1, npm 12.2.1, tailwindcss 0.0.0-insiders.a3cb19c, @tailwindcss/node 0.0.0-insiders.a3cb19c, @tailwindcss/oxide 0.0.0-insiders.a3cb19c, typescript 7.0.2
index.ts(5,94): error TS4104: The type 'readonly SourceEntry[]' is 'readonly' and cannot be assigned to the mutable type 'SourceEntry[]'.
index.ts(9,25): error TS4104: The type 'readonly string[]' is 'readonly' and cannot be assigned to the mutable type 'string[]'.
index.ts(14,25): error TS4104: The type 'readonly string[]' is 'readonly' and cannot be assigned to the mutable type 'string[]'.
SUMMARY: defect: 3 call(s) refuse a readonly array, taking only a mutable one
```

`npm run check` exits 1 while any of the three refuses the readonly array and 0 once `index.ts` type-checks. The declarations come from `crates/node/src/lib.rs` (`pub sources: Option<Vec<SourceEntry>>`, which NAPI-RS writes as `Array<SourceEntry>`) and `packages/tailwindcss/src/index.ts` (`build(candidates: string[])`).

Issues.Title: Reduce the size of `@tailwindcss/browser` and only scan the elements that changed
Issues.Body:
## Summary

This PR makes `@tailwindcss/browser` smaller, and makes it do less work on every DOM change.

|          |    Before |     After |        |
| -------- | --------: | --------: | -----: |
| Minified | 295,631 B | 230,193 B | −22.1% |
| Gzip     |  78,228 B |  60,367 B | −22.8% |
| Brotli   |  63,971 B |  51,423 B | −19.6% |

### Build-time switches in core

Most of the size was code that can never run in the browser. Core now has two build-time switches, documented in `packages/tailwindcss/src/node.d.ts`:

- `TAILWIND_INTELLISENSE`: class and variant suggestions, and canonicalization.
- `TAILWIND_JS_PLUGINS`: `@plugin`, `@config`, and the JS theme they rely on.

The code checks `process.env.TAILWIND_… !== 'false'` right where it is used. The published `tailwindcss` build defines both switches as `"true"`, so it does not change. `@tailwindcss/browser` defines both as `"false"`, and esbuild removes the code. This replaces the `patch-intellisense-apis` esbuild plugin, which replaced modules by file path.

Two more things happen in the `tsup.config.ts` of the browser build:

- Every bundled module is marked as free of side effects. Without this, esbuild keeps the v3 default theme in the bundle because of its top-level object spreads, even when nothing uses it.
- The embedded stylesheets (`preflight.css`, `theme.css`, …) are minified with the CSS parser of core. The build fails when a minified stylesheet does not parse back to the same AST.

### Runtime

- On a DOM change, only the elements in the mutation records are checked for new classes, instead of `document.querySelectorAll('[class]')`. On a page with 603 elements, a class change on two elements now reads 2 class attributes instead of 604. A change to a stylesheet still scans the whole document.
- The stylesheet is not written when the generated CSS did not change.
- A failed build no longer prevents all later builds. Before, the build queue stayed rejected after the first error (e.g. an `@apply` with a class that does not exist), and the page did not get new CSS until a reload.

### Behavior changes in `@tailwindcss/browser`

- Legacy `theme()` paths only resolve when they map to a theme variable, because the JS theme is not in the bundle anymore. `theme(colors.red.500)`, `theme(colors.red.500 / 50%)`, `theme(screens.md)` and `theme(fontSize.sm)` still work. `theme(spacing.4)`, `theme(opacity.50)` and `theme(zIndex.10)` now fail with "Could not resolve value for theme function", unless they have a fallback. `theme(blur.sm)` now resolves to the v4 value (`8px`) instead of the v3 value (`4px`).
- The error for `@plugin` and `@config` is now "This build of Tailwind CSS does not support `@plugin` or `@config`."

To get the old `theme()` behavior back, set `TAILWIND_JS_PLUGINS` to `"true"` in `packages/@tailwindcss-browser/tsup.config.ts`. This adds about 14 KB gzipped.

## Test plan

- Added `packages/tailwindcss/src/build-switches.test.ts`. It checks that the generated CSS for more than 10,000 candidates is the same with the switches turned off, and covers the behavior of each switch.
- Added `packages/@tailwindcss-browser/src/bundle.test.ts`. It builds the real bundle and fails when IntelliSense, the JS plugin API, JS config files or the default JS theme end up in it, when `process.env` is left in it, or when it grows past 64,000 bytes gzipped.
- The test suite of `tailwindcss` passes (5,407 tests).
- Built `tailwindcss` and checked that the published build still has suggestions, canonicalization and plugin support, and no `process.env.TAILWIND_…` left in it.
- Compared the old and the new bundle in a stand-in DOM in Node: they generate the same CSS (apart from one space in an `@supports` rule of Preflight).
- Added three Playwright tests to `packages/@tailwindcss-browser/tests/ui.spec.ts`: elements inside of new elements, recovering from invalid CSS, and legacy `theme()` paths. **The Playwright suite was not run locally** (Chromium could not be started in the sandbox this was written in), so these tests run for the first time on CI.
- The timings were not measured in a real browser. In Node, the time until the first CSS went down by about 6%.

Issues.Title: Ignore arbitrary values that start a CSS comment
Issues.Body:
This PR fixes an issue where a `/*` in an arbitrary value could comment out the CSS that comes after it.

A candidate like `bg-[red/*]` or `[color:red/*]` passed validation, and generated this CSS:

```css
.bg-\[red\/\*\] {
  background-color: red/*;
}
.underline {
  text-decoration-line: underline;
}
```

The `/*` starts a comment that never ends. Browsers ignore the CSS up to the next `*/`, and Lightning CSS drops all the rules after it. So one stray candidate in a scanned file (for example in a code sample or a comment) could silently remove other utilities, like `.underline` here, from the output.

`isValidArbitrary` now rejects a `/*` outside of a string or an unquoted `url(…)`. This applies to arbitrary values, arbitrary properties, arbitrary modifiers and arbitrary variants, because they all go through this function. A complete comment like `bg-[red/*x*/]` is valid CSS, but no candidate needs one, so we reject it too and keep the check simple. A `/*` inside of a string stays valid, for example `content-['/*']` or `bg-[url('/*.png')]`. An escaped `\/*` is rejected too, because PostCSS reads it as the start of a comment.

## A `/*` in an unquoted `url(…)`

In CSS, an unquoted `url(…)` is a single token, so a `/*` inside of it is not a comment. These stay valid:

- `bg-[url(/a/*.png)]`
- `bg-[url(a.png),_url(/b/*.png)]`
- `bg-[image-set(url(/a/*.png)_1x)]`
- `bg-[no-repeat_url(/a/*.png)]`
- `bg-[image:url(/a/*.png)]`
- `[background-image:url(/a/*.png)]`

The PostCSS tokenizer reads a `url(…)` only in some positions. So we allow a `/*` only in a lowercase `url(` that is not followed by whitespace, and that starts the value, or comes after whitespace (or an `_`), a `(` or a type hint like `image:`. This only applies to values that end up in a declaration (utility values and arbitrary properties), not to modifiers and variants. Other forms like `URL(/a/*.png)`, `#url(/a/*.png)` or `@image:url(/a/*.png)` are rejected.

The gradient utilities now print a space after the `,` in `var(--tw-gradient-stops, …)`, so PostCSS does not read `,url(` as one word.

Known limitation: a minifier like Lightning CSS removes the space after a `,`, and PostCSS then reads `,url(/b/*.png)` as the start of a comment. This also happens for plain CSS like `url(a.png), url("/b/*.png")`, and is reported upstream in https://github.com/postcss/postcss/issues/2194.

## Test plan

- Added `bg-[red/*]`, `bg-[red/*comment*/]`, `[color:red/*]`, `bg-red-500/[50%/*]`, `[&/*]:flex` and `data-[a/*]:flex` to the invalid candidates in `candidate.test.ts`. They fail without this change.
- Added the unsafe `url(…)` forms to the invalid candidates, and tests that the safe forms above still parse.
- Added a test that `content-['/*']` still parses.
- Added a test with 5000 seeded random arbitrary values. Each generated CSS goes through Lightning CSS, and a rule after it must survive.
- Built `bg-[red/*] flex underline [color:red/*]` and ran the result through Lightning CSS. Before: all rules after `.bg-\[red\/\*\]` were gone, `.underline` too. After: `.flex` and `.underline` are there, and the invalid candidates are ignored.

Issues.Title: Improve performance when scanning long lines with arbitrary values or variants that don't end
Issues.Body:
## Summary

This PR continues https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20694. The Oxide extractor took quadratic time on more shapes of long lines. For example, on `main`, a line of 80 KB with `p-4*` repeated takes 580 ms.

This is hardening. No open issue reports these shapes. The most realistic case that I found is a minified JS data module: one long line with many empty arrays, and strings without spaces. For example `[{"id":"a1","tags":[],"ref":"x"},…]` in a `.js` file. The JSON pre-processor does not run on `.js` files, so the `[` and `]` stay. For a file of 1 MB like this, the extractor takes 9.3 s on `main` and 8.5 ms with this PR (release build).

There are two causes:

1. An arbitrary value that doesn't close scans to the end of the line. The extractor starts an arbitrary value at each `[`, so a long line with many of them takes quadratic time. For example:
   - `[]"a"[]"a"…`, because an arbitrary value can't be empty, so the first `]` doesn't close it.
   - `[\[\[\…`, because of the escaped characters.
   - Minified data with empty arrays, like `{"tags":[],"cls":"flex"},…`.
   - `a/[]"a"a/[]"a"…`, the same in the arbitrary value of a modifier.
2. A named variant that doesn't end scans to the end of the line for a `:`. For example, in `p-4*p-4*…`, the variant that starts at each `p` goes to the end of the line, because `*` is valid in a variant.

This PR fixes both, and the extracted candidates do not change:

1. Without open brackets, the rest of an arbitrary value depends only on the position, not on where it started. The only exception is right after the `[`, where a `]` doesn't close it. So `ArbitraryValueMemo` remembers, for each position, where the arbitrary value that went through it stopped. A later arbitrary value that gets to the same position without open brackets stops there too.
   - `VariantMachine`, `NamedVariantMachine`, `NamedUtilityMachine` and `UtilityMachine` (for modifiers) each have a memo.
   - They use it only from 64 characters after the `[`, so most lines don't need one. The first 64 characters have a loop of their own, without the checks of the memo. The loop with the memo is a separate function that is not inlined, so short arbitrary values keep the same code as on `main`.
   - The memo starts at the first position that it uses, so a long arbitrary value at the end of a full file (like in `@tailwindcss/upgrade`) doesn't allocate memory for the start of the file.
2. Each step of a named variant moves one character, and depends only on the input. So the machine remembers the range that the last variant went through. A variant that starts in that range skips to where the last variant stopped.

The first commit also sets the start of single-character variants (e.g. `a:`) in `NamedVariantMachine`. Before, their span started where the previous variant started. `VariantMachine` uses its own start, so the candidates don't change. But the new tests compare a machine that already ran on a line with a new machine, and these spans were different.

### Cost

Measured with a release build (`lto = true`) that has one copy of the extractor, like the published package:

- 25M lines from 166K real files (1.5 GB): 7.06 s on `main`, 7.35 s with this PR (about 4% more).
- The memo uses 4 bytes for each position after its first one, but only on lines with an arbitrary value of more than 64 characters. For the longest line in the files that I tested (a source map of 4.5 MB), the peak memory goes from 14 MB to 30 MB.
- `[[A[[A…` is still quadratic, as on `main`, with the same time (80 KB: 820 ms on `main`, 860 ms with this PR). The cause is not in the arbitrary values: `SubCandidateExtractor` scans to the end of the line from each range. This PR does not change that.

### Times

For one line of 80 KB:

| Input | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[]"a"` repeated | 275 ms | 1.5 ms |
| `[\` repeated | 563 ms | 1.9 ms |
| `p-4*` repeated | 606 ms | 0.3 ms |
| `bg-[]"a"` repeated | 362 ms | 2.2 ms |
| `[]a[]b` repeated | 580 ms | 2.5 ms |
| `a/[]a` repeated | 660 ms | 2.5 ms |
| `{"id":1,"tags":[],"cls":"flex"},` repeated | 42 ms | 0.7 ms |

## Test plan

- Added `test_long_lines_with_empty_arbitrary_values`, and more lines in `test_long_lines_without_candidates`. Each line must take less than 5 s. On `main`, both tests fail: the first new line of each takes 16 s and 19 s in a debug build. With this PR, all extractor tests take about 0.7 s.
- Added a `test_reuse` helper. It checks that a machine that already ran on a line finds the same result from each position as a new machine. The tests of `VariantMachine`, `NamedVariantMachine`, `NamedUtilityMachine` and `UtilityMachine` use it on long lines, and `test_reuse_machines_on_random_lines` uses it on 500 random lines.
- Added `test_arbitrary_value_machine_memo`. It compares the arbitrary values with and without the memo, from each position, in both orders. `test_arbitrary_value_machine_memo_size` checks that the memo doesn't grow for the positions before its first one.
- I compared the extracted candidates (spans and order) of this PR with those of `main`. They are the same for:
  - 25M lines from 166K real files (1.5 GB). Most of the files come from `node_modules`, with many minified bundles and source maps.

Issues.Title: Improve `@tailwindcss/vite` build performance by scanning the same sources only once per build
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Hi, and thanks for maintaining Tailwind CSS.
While profiling `react-router build` in our React Router app, I found that Tailwind scanned the project for the client build, scanned it again for the SSR build, and walked it once more each time to collect files to watch, although a build doesn't watch anything.

Outside of watch mode, this:

- shares the scanned candidates between roots and environments with the same sources in a build. React Router (with the Vite Environment API), SvelteKit, TanStack Start and SolidStart build their environments with the same plugin instance (`builder.sharedPlugins`), so the SSR build no longer scans again.
- stops reading `scanner.files` and `scanner.globs` just to call `addWatchFile()`. Reading `globs` walks the sources again.
- doesn't create a `Scanner` for stylesheets that aren't Tailwind roots.

On our app (5,971 files to scan, React Router 8.5.1, Vite 8.3.6, macOS), `react-router build` goes from 15.9 s to 13.2 s with identical output: the client build from 8.6 s to 7.8 s, and the SSR build from 6.5 s to 4.6 s.
In a Linux container, the same files take 125 ms to scan and 21 ms for `globs`, so the saving there is about 170 ms per build.

This also keeps the SSR CSS the same as the client CSS.
When `build/` isn't ignored, the SSR scan picked up the client build output, and React Router emitted a second stylesheet with a different hash, which looks like #19888.

Dev mode and `vite build --watch` behave as before, including workers built during a watched build.
The shared candidates are reset in `configResolved` and when an environment builds again, and only the first scan of a new scanner is shared.
The `source(…)` check still throws in the same cases.

[ci-all]

## Test plan

- The new React Router integration test builds with `v8_viteEnvironmentApi` and without `build/` in `.gitignore`, and expects one stylesheet. It fails on `main` and passes here.
- `pnpm run test:integrations ./integrations/vite` passes, and so does the `watch mode` test with its fixture switched to Vite 8.
- The 57 CSS files emitted by the 51 building integration tests are identical to `main`, apart from the extra stylesheet in the new test.
- In small Vite 8 fixtures, a `source()` listing files, a worker in `worker.plugins` during `vite build --watch`, a reused builder and a reused plugin instance all give the same CSS as `main`.
- `pnpm test` and `pnpm changelog check` pass.

Issues.Title: Ensure `@tailwindcss/vite` rebuilds when a plugin changes the input CSS in memory
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`@tailwindcss/vite` reuses its compiler when the mtimes of the build dependencies (the input file and its `@import`/`@config`/`@plugin` graph) did not change. It never compares the CSS that it receives in `transform`. So when a plugin that runs before Tailwind changes the CSS in memory, and no file of the stylesheet changes on disk, Tailwind returns CSS from the old input.

An example: a plugin with `enforce: 'pre'` inlines `src/partial.css` into `src/index.css` and calls `this.addWatchFile()`. After an edit of `src/partial.css`, Vite transforms `src/index.css` again, but the CSS still has the old partial. This happens in `vite dev`, in `vite build --watch`, and in a kept `createBuilder()` builder that builds again.

This PR keeps the input CSS of the last compiler setup on the `Root`, and sets up the compiler again when the input differs. The first transform does no extra work, because there is no compiler yet.

This is the same fix as for `@tailwindcss/postcss` in https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20310, and for `@tailwindcss/webpack` and `@tailwindcss/turbopack` in https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20582.

## Test plan

- Added integration tests in `integrations/vite/other-transforms.test.ts` for `vite dev`, `vite build --watch`, and a `createBuilder()` builder that builds `client` two times. A plugin before Tailwind inlines a partial in memory, and each test changes the partial from `red` to `blue`.
- Confirmed that all three fail on `main` (the CSS keeps `color: red`), and pass with the fix.
- Ran the other tests in `integrations/vite/other-transforms.test.ts`, and the other Vite integration tests, and `pnpm run build`.

Issues.Title: Don't treat `/*` inside an unquoted `url(…)` as a comment in the CSS parser
Issues.Body:
This PR fixes a bug in our CSS parser where a `/*` inside an unquoted `url(…)` was treated as the start of a comment.

Per [CSS Syntax 3](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-syntax-3/#consume-ident-like-token), `url(` (case-insensitive) followed by a character that is not a quote starts a single url token, which ends at the first unescaped `)`. Comments are only recognized at the start of a token, so a `/*` inside of the url is just text.

Before this change:

```css
/* Input */
.a { background-image: url(/b/*.png); }
.b { color: red; }

/* Output: the url silently lost a `/` */
.a { background-image: url(/b*.png); }
.b { color: red; }
```

And when a real comment followed later in the file, the "comment" ran until that comment's `*/` and the parser threw `Missing closing } at .a`. The same happened in at-rule params (e.g. `@import url(/b/*.css);`), and in custom properties when a comment followed.

The fix is small: when the parser sees a `(` that follows the ident `url`, and the next non-whitespace character is not a quote, it consumes everything up to the first unescaped `)` as one unit. This is done in the main loop (declarations, selectors, at-rules) and in the custom property loop. A quoted `url("…")` is a regular function with a string, and keeps the existing behavior. A function like `my-url(…)` is not a url token either.

A quote or `(` inside of an unquoted url makes a "bad url" per spec. This PR keeps the current behavior for those.

Related: https://github.com/postcss/postcss/issues/2194, the same class of bug in PostCSS.

## Test plan

Added tests to `css-parser.test.ts`, which fail without this change:

- `url(/b/*.png)` keeps its `/`
- A comment after `url(/b/*.png)` does not throw
- `URL(/b/*.png)`, `url( /b/*.png )`, and `url(a.png),url(/b/*.png)`
- An at-rule param with an unquoted url
- A custom property with an unquoted url, followed by a comment

And two tests to guard existing behavior: a real comment next to a `url(…)` is still removed, and a `/*` inside of `my-url(…)` is still a comment.

Issues.Title: Replace CSS escapes that are not needed during canonicalization
Issues.Body:
`canonicalizeCandidates` now replaces CSS escapes in `[…]` with the character that they stand for, if the escape is not needed:

```
bg-[u\72l('a.png')]  → bg-[url('a.png')]
bg-[u\72_l('a.png')] → bg-[url('a.png')]
[\63olor:red]        → text-[red]
[&_.f\6f_o]:flex     → [&_.foo]:flex
```

This covers arbitrary values, arbitrary properties, arbitrary variants and arbitrary modifiers (everything in `[…]`). It does not cover the `(…)` shorthand, like `bg-(--my\-color)`.

## What we replace

Escapes of ASCII letters, digits and `-` in a name, and only if the CSS stays the same. A hex escape has up to 6 hex digits and one optional whitespace after them. In a candidate, an `_` is that whitespace.

## What we keep

- `\_`, because it is a literal `_` in a candidate.
- Escapes in strings, e.g. `content-['\61']`.
- Escapes of characters that are not name characters, e.g. `\,`, `\)` or `\2c`.
- Escapes that make a name out of something else. E.g.: `\31_0` is the name `10`, but `10` is a number. `1\65_3` is `1` with the unit `e3`, but `1e3` is `1000`. `\-1` is a name, but `-1` is a number.
- An escape if a hex digit comes after the escape before it. E.g. the `\61` in `\31\61`, because `\31a` is one escape.
- An escape if `-->` or `<!--` would take part of the name, e.g. `-\->`.
- A hex escape with an `_` after it, if the `_` might not be a space. `decodeArbitraryValue` keeps an `_` in a `url(…)` and in the first argument of `var(…)` and `theme(…)`, and an arbitrary property name is not decoded at all. E.g. `bg-[url(\61_b.png)]` stays as it is.
- The escapes in a function name that would become `url`, `var` or `theme`, if the function has an `_` in it. E.g. `bg-[u\72l(a_b.png)]` stays as it is, because the `_` would not be a space anymore in `url(a_b.png)`.

Tailwind reads function names as written, so `c\61lc(1+2)` gets no math operator spacing today, but `calc(1+2)` does. CSS reads both as `calc(…)`, so the new candidate does what the escaped one was meant to do.

## Interaction with the PR that ignores CSS comments

https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20690 rejects a function name with a CSS escape in it, like `bg-[u\72l('a.png')]`, because `u\72l(foo'bar)/*')` could start a CSS comment. After it merges, such a candidate does not parse, and canonicalization could not suggest anything.

So this replacement runs on the raw candidate, before the parse. We use the new candidate only if it parses, and canonicalize it further from there. I tested both cases:

| Candidate | `main` + this PR | With https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20690 + this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bg-[u\72l('a.png')]` | parses, → `bg-[url('a.png')]` | does not parse, → `bg-[url('a.png')]` |
| `bg-[u\72_l('a.png')]` | parses, → `bg-[url('a.png')]` | does not parse, → `bg-[url('a.png')]` |
| `bg-[u\72l(foo'bar)/*')]` | parses, → `bg-[url(foo'bar)/*')]` | does not parse, stays as it is |
| `bg-[u\72l(a_b.png)]` | parses, stays as it is | does not parse, stays as it is |

On `main`, the third candidate already produces the comment, with or without this PR. With https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20690, the new candidate does not parse either, so we keep the old one.

The two PRs do not change the same files, and can merge in any order.

## Test plan

- Example tests in `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts`, for each strategy (default, with a variant, important, prefix).
- A seeded random test: it builds 20,000 values from escaped and plain pieces, in a value, a property name and a selector. It compares the CSS before and after, minified by Lightning CSS, which decodes escapes and keeps only the needed ones. When I turn off one of the rules, this test fails. It found the `<!--` case. I also ran it with 4 other seeds and 200,000 values each.
- With the commits of https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20690 cherry-picked, `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts` and `candidate.test.ts` pass.
- `pnpm run build`, and all tests of `packages/tailwindcss`.

Issues.Title: Use the incremental build when `from` is set
Issues.Body:
This PR builds on https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20680, and targets its branch. Merge that one first.

## Summary

The incremental build of https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20680 is turned off when `from` is set. The CLI with `--output`, `@tailwindcss/postcss`, `@tailwindcss/webpack`, `@tailwindcss/turbopack` and `@tailwindcss/vite` with CSS source maps all set `from`, so they don't get the faster rebuilds.

These integrations need `from` for source maps, and for the file, line and column in CSS syntax errors (https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/19282). So the fix is in core, and the integrations don't change:

- The incremental build gives new utility nodes the source location of `@tailwind utilities` before it caches them, the same way the non-incremental build does.
- `build()` no longer tracks the positions in the output, so it can reuse the printed CSS of the cached utilities. `buildSourceMap()` tracks them instead, once for each build. The printed CSS is the same, and all callers ask for the source map right after `build()`.

## Performance

Rebuilds on tailwindcss.com that add one class (median of 600 builds):

| Build | `main` | https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20680 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `compile()` with `from` (CLI with `--output`, webpack, Turbopack) | 11.8 ms | 11.8 ms | 1.2–1.5 ms |
| `compile()` with `from`, and a source map after each build (CLI with `--map`, Vite) | 18.4 ms | 17.4 ms | 7.4–8.8 ms |
| `compileAst()` with `from` (PostCSS, without its conversion to a PostCSS AST) | 11.4 ms | — | 1.7 ms |

With this PR, a build with `from` is as fast as a build without it (about 1.1 ms). With source maps, `createSourceMap()` is now most of the time.

## Test plan

- `incremental.test.ts` used `from` to get the non-incremental build to compare against. It now loads a second copy of the modules where the incremental build is mocked away. It runs with and without `from`, and with `from` it also compares the source maps. Without the fix, 7 tests fail.
- A new test in `source-map.test.ts` does several builds, and compares each source map with the source map of a new compiler. It fails when the positions are out of date.
- The `tailwindcss`, `@tailwindcss/postcss` and `@tailwindcss/node` tests pass.
- Locally, the integration tests pass for Vite source maps, and for the watch mode, source map and parse error tests of `@tailwindcss/cli` and `@tailwindcss/postcss`.

Issues.Title: Only optimize and print new utilities on rebuilds
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The AST of each candidate is already cached by the design system, but when a single new candidate shows up, `build()` still re-sorts every rule and runs `optimizeAst`, `handleNesting` and `toCss` over the entire stylesheet. `handleNesting` also re-parses every selector, because its parse cache only lives for one call. So the cost of a rebuild grows with the size of the stylesheet instead of the size of the change.

Profile of a rebuild that adds one class, on the [tailwindcss.com](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss.com) repo (13.6k scanned candidates, 716 KB of CSS):

| Step | Time |
| --- | --- |
| Re-sort all rules (`compileCandidates`) | 3.2 ms |
| `optimizeAst` on the whole stylesheet | 3.7 ms |
| `handleNesting` on the whole stylesheet | 4.8 ms |
| `toCss` on the whole stylesheet | 1.0 ms |

This PR adds an incremental path for the utilities (`packages/tailwindcss/src/incremental.ts`):

1. Only the new candidates are compiled and sorted. They're merged into the list of already sorted candidates. When new variants show up, the variant bits of existing candidates are updated: new variants can shift the bits, but never the relative order of candidates we already sorted.
2. The optimized and flattened output of each utility node is cached, keyed by the AST node the design system already caches. A build stitches the cached output together, merging adjacent at-rules (e.g. `@media`) and rules with the same selector, the same way `handleNesting` does. Cached nodes are copied before they're merged into, never mutated.
3. The rest of the stylesheet still goes through `optimizeAst` on every build, with a placeholder where the utilities go. The `@at-root` nodes (`@property`, `@keyframes`) and the `animation` values of the utilities are passed along, so `@property` deduplication, the `@property` polyfill and unused `@keyframes` removal work as before.
4. `toCss` caches the printed CSS of the cached nodes.

Rules that only contain declarations (most utilities) skip `optimizeAst`/`handleNesting` entirely, so the per-utility setup cost doesn't slow down the initial build.

The output should be byte-for-byte identical to the non-incremental build. We fall back to the non-incremental build when:
- source maps are requested (`from`), because `toCss` needs the positions of every node in the current build
- `@tailwind utilities` is somewhere we can't handle (e.g. inside a rule, or in a context like `@theme`)
- something unexpected comes up during a build

### Results

Same project, Node 24, Apple Silicon. Rebuild numbers are the median of 300 rebuilds:

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rebuild that adds 1 class (tailwindcss.com) | 12.6 ms | 1.4 ms |
| Rebuild that adds 1 class (`@import "tailwindcss"`) | 9.2 ms | 1.1 ms |
| Rebuild that adds a class with a new variant | 15.0 ms | 2.8–4.1 ms |
| Initial build, warm JIT | ~37 ms | ~38 ms |
| Initial build, fresh process | ~68 ms | ~75 ms |

### Open questions

- **Cold initial build** is ~10% slower in a fresh process. It's the same once the JIT is warm, so it's likely from the extra code paths warming up. Worth looking at before merging.
- **PostCSS** always passes `from`, so `@tailwindcss/postcss` doesn't benefit yet. The same goes for Vite with `css.devSourcemap`. The non-incremental build only needs `from` for `toCss` source map tracking, so a follow-up could make that check narrower.
- **Follow-up for Vite:** the Vite plugin re-walks the whole project with `scanner.scan()` on every CSS request (7.7 ms on the same project). Scanning only the changed file with `scanner.scanFiles()` takes 0.3 ms. Together with this PR, that would take Tailwind's share of an HMR update from ~20 ms to ~2 ms.

## Test plan

- Added `packages/tailwindcss/src/incremental.test.ts`. It compares the incremental build with the non-incremental build (`from` set) across several inputs and orders of adding candidates, covering:
  - inputs: default, without layers, `important` + `theme(static)`, custom `@utility`/`@custom-variant`/`@keyframes` with sibling rules in `@layer utilities`, and utilities nested in a rule (the fallback)
  - candidates: variants, stacked variants, at-rule merging, `@property`, `@keyframes`, `color-mix(…)` polyfills, arbitrary values/properties, important, invalid candidates, and CSS variables used outside of utilities
- Checked that the tests fail when the at-rule merging or the copy-on-write of cached nodes is removed.
- `vitest run --hideSkippedTests` from the root: 5722 passed, 1 skipped. Rust isn't installed on my machine, so I didn't run `cargo test` or build oxide. For the JS packages that need `@tailwindcss/oxide`, I used the published 4.3.5 binary; this PR doesn't touch Rust.
- `tsc --noEmit` reports the same errors as on `main` (all from missing build artifacts locally), and `prettier --check` / `pnpm changelog check` pass.
- Outside of the test suite, I compared the CSS of the incremental and non-incremental builds for 1281 incremental builds on the tailwindcss.com candidates, across 7 inputs (including `prefix(tw)`) and random orders and batch sizes: no differences.

Issues.Title: Avoid climbing across Windows drives when rebasing URLs in stylesheets
Issues.Body:
Fixes #20682.

## Summary

When an entry stylesheet and an imported stylesheet are located on different Windows drive letters (or different UNC shares), `path.posix.relative` treats drive letters as regular directory names. This causes `rebaseUrl` to emit a drive-climbing path like `url("../../../../../../../H:/.../images/probe.svg")` when trying to relate paths across drives.

In this PR:
- Detect when `root` and `base` have different roots (such as different Windows drive letters or UNC shares) using `path.win32.parse()`. When they are on different drives, there is no valid relative path between them, so `rebaseUrl` preserves the resolved absolute URL.
- Normalize drive letter casing so same-drive comparisons (e.g. `c:` vs `C:`) continue to rebase relatively without generating `../` prefixes.
- Return already-absolute Windows paths early, matching the existing behavior for `/` root paths.

## Test plan

Added unit tests in `packages/@tailwindcss-node/src/urls.test.ts`:
- Tested cross-drive URL rewriting (`C:` root with `H:` base) to verify the absolute URL is retained.
- Tested same-drive URL rewriting with differing drive letter casing (`c:` vs `C:`) to ensure relative rebasing is preserved.
- Tested parent directory navigation (`../`) on cross-drive stylesheets to ensure resolution keeps the correct path.
- Tested already-absolute Windows drive paths in `url()` to verify they are preserved.

Ran vitest across `@tailwindcss-node`:
All 12 tests in `@tailwindcss-node` passed.

Issues.Title: Improve performance when scanning long lines with many `[` characters
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The Oxide extractor took quadratic time on some long lines. Minified files and generated content often have long lines, so this can slow down the scan of a real project. For example, on `main`, a line of 80 KB with only `[` characters takes 3.2 s.

There are two causes:

1. When the main candidate machine consumes a range, the extractor starts a new candidate machine after each `[` in that range, to find the candidates inside the brackets (e.g. `[ClassPrefix('gap-y-4')]`). Each machine runs until the end of the range. Thus a long line with many `[` takes quadratic time.
2. On a `<` or an uppercase letter, the candidate machine searches the rest of the line for a boundary character. If the line has none, the machine restarts at the next character, and searches the same bytes again.

This PR fixes both, and the extracted candidates do not change:

1. The candidate machine now reports each position where it starts from a clean state (no variant in progress). From such a position, the machine finds the same candidates, no matter where it started. Thus when a machine reaches a position where an earlier machine of the same range was in a clean state, it stops: the earlier machine already found the candidates from there.
2. The candidate machine remembers the position from which the line has no boundary, and a later search stops there.

Times for one line of 80 KB, with an optimized build:

| Input | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[` repeated | 3.24 s | 3.5 ms |
| `a-[` repeated | 1.45 s | 3.9 ms |
| `"a-['` repeated | 576 ms | 6.5 ms |
| `a-[a]-[a]…` | 2.14 s | 0.8 ms |
| `<%= a-[` repeated | 877 ms | 0.5 ms |

## Test plan

- Added `test_long_lines_without_candidates`. It checks that long lines of these shapes give no candidates, and that each line takes less than 5 s. On `main`, the first line alone takes 89 s in a debug build. With this PR, the full test takes about 0.5 s.
- Added `test_overlapping_candidates_in_long_lines`. It checks the candidates in nested arrays on a long line (e.g. minified JSON).
- I compared the extracted candidates (spans and order) of this PR with those of `main`. They are the same for:
  - 82.8M lines from 310K real files (4.7 GB). Most of the files come from `node_modules`, with many minified bundles and source maps. On the same lines, the total time went from 23.1 s to 20.2 s.
  - More than 10M random inputs, made of tokens like `[`, `]`, `\`, quotes, `hover:`, `bg-[` and `[&`.
  - 20K random short patterns, each repeated to 10 KB.
- `cargo test` in `crates/oxide`, `pnpm run build`, and `vitest` pass.

Issues.Title: Discard candidates whose selectors grow exponentially when variants are stacked
Issues.Body:
## Summary

When the nesting of a rule is flattened, each `&` is replaced with the parent selector, and each selector in a selector list without `&` gets the parent selector as a prefix. Stacked variants therefore multiply the length of the selectors. A pathological candidate like `[&_&]:[&_&]:[&_&]:…:flex` doubles the CSS with each variant:

| `[&_&]:` variants | Time | CSS |
| --: | --: | --: |
| 12 | 20 ms | 0.58 MB |
| 14 | 54 ms | 2.66 MB |
| 16 | 203 ms | 12 MB |
| 20 | out of memory | |

Selector lists (`[&,.a]:`, or `@custom-variant hocus (&:hover, &:focus)`) and custom variants with multiple `@slot`s grow in the same way. The scanner extracts such candidates from any text, so a single class name in a source file (or in a page that uses `@tailwindcss/browser`) is enough to stop the build.

This PR estimates the length of the flattened selectors of a candidate after its variants are applied, without generating them, and discards the candidate when the estimate is above 1,000,000 characters. The candidate is then invalid, like an unknown utility.

The estimate is computed for each node as `a * P + b`, where `P` is the length of the parent selector. This makes it linear in the size of the AST, also when variants with multiple `@slot`s re-use the same nodes. It stays within about 2× of the real output for the patterns above.

The limit is far above real candidates:

- The largest estimate in the test suite (882,614 compiled candidates) is 1,737 characters.
- `prose` from `@tailwindcss/typography` is about 8,000, and about 35,000 with 10 variants.
- Just below the limit, a candidate still compiles in about 20 ms, with up to about 0.6 MB of CSS.

The generated CSS of candidates below the limit does not change.

## Test plan

- Added a test that `[&_&]:`, `[&,.a]:`, a selector list variant and a variant with two `@slot`s, each stacked 20 times, generate nothing. Without the limit, the test runs out of memory.

Issues.Title: Improve performance of candidates with long variant chains
Issues.Body:
This PR makes parsing and compiling pathological candidates with long variant chains fast, instead of taking seconds or exceeding the call stack.

Such candidates don't appear in real projects, but the scanner extracts candidates of any length from the content files. So a single generated or minified file can contain one, and then the whole build hangs or crashes.

Some numbers in Node, measured with `compiler.build([candidate])`:

| Candidate | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `not-` × 1000 + `hover:flex` | 832 ms | 1 ms |
| `not-` × 2000 + `hover:flex` | 6.4 s, then `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` | 0 ms |
| `group-` × 1000 + `hover:flex` | 1.2 s | 0 ms |
| `hover:` × 1000 + `flex` | `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` | 0 ms |

There are three separate problems, one per commit:

1. **`findRoots` is quadratic.** It tests the part before each dash as a root, from the last dash to the first. For an input with many dashes (e.g. `data-a-a-…-a`), this looks up a long prefix for every dash. A compound variant parses its sub-variant in the same way, so a chain of compound variants was cubic. Roots that are longer than the longest registered name can't exist, so we now start at the last dash that can end one. `Variants` and `Utilities` keep track of the longest name. The result doesn't change.

2. **Compound variants recurse once for each level.** A variant like `in-in-in-…-hover` with a few thousand levels exceeds the call stack. Variants can now nest at most 16 compound variants. Real variants only nest a few (e.g. `not-group-has-peer-hover` nests 4).

   The sub-variant is parsed through the cache of the design system, and `Variants.compare` relies on sub-variants being the same objects, so the sub-variants have to stay cached. A plain counter would then cache the inner levels of a chain that is too deep as invalid, even though they can be valid on their own (e.g. `in-hover`). So at the limit we throw a sentinel, and only the outermost compound variant returns `null`. A sub-variant can also come from the cache, so we count its compound variants too. This way, the result doesn't depend on what was parsed before.

3. **Each stacked variant nests the CSS one level deeper.** `hover:` × 1000 + `flex` exceeds the call stack in `optimizeAst`. Below that, the indentation makes the output quadratic (`hover:` × 4000 generated 32 MB of CSS). Candidates can now stack at most 64 variants. The prefix doesn't count.

The limits are far above what real candidates use, and arbitrary values are not limited, so long values like data URIs still work.

## Test plan

- Added tests in `candidate.test.ts`:
  - Variants and utilities with many dashes parse in linear time.
  - 16 nested compound variants parse, 17 don't, and a chain of 10,000 bails out early.
  - Parsing a chain that is too deep doesn't make the variants inside of it invalid, and a cached inner variant doesn't make a chain that is too deep valid.
  - 64 stacked variants parse, 65 don't, and the prefix doesn't count.
- Added tests in `variants.test.ts` with the default variants: `not-group-has-peer-hover:flex` still works, and chains that are too deep or stack too many variants generate no CSS (they crashed before).
- Each new test fails without its commit.
- `pnpm run build` and all vitest tests pass.

Issues.Title: Discard candidates that contain `</style`
Issues.Body:
This PR discards candidates that contain `</style`, so that the generated CSS is always safe to inline in a `<style>` element.

Some frameworks inline the generated CSS in a `<style>` element (for example Nuxt, Astro with `inlineStylesheets`, or Next.js with `inlineCss`). The HTML parser ends a `<style>` element at `</style`, so a candidate like `content-['</style>']` ends that element early. These forms could all put `</style` in the output:

- Arbitrary values: `before:content-['</style>']`, `font-[x</style>]`
- Arbitrary properties: `[--x:</style>]`, `[--x</style>:red]`
- Arbitrary variants: `[&[data-x="</style>"]]:flex`
- Arbitrary modifiers: `bg-red-500/[</style>]`

The class name part of the selector was already safe, because it is escaped.

## Approach

Only arbitrary parts can put text from the candidate in the output as-is. Named roots, values and modifiers must match a known utility, variant or theme key. So the check lives in `isValidArbitrary`, which already validates each arbitrary value, variant, modifier and arbitrary property name.

After the existing checks pass, `isValidArbitrary` decodes the value and looks for `</style` (case insensitive). A value without a `<` or a `\` skips the decode, so most candidates do no extra work.

Escaping the output instead is not enough, because Lightning CSS decodes escapes when it minifies the CSS. So the check decodes the value the same way first:

- CSS escapes: `\3c /style`, `\3C/STYLE` and `<\/style`
- Escaped newlines, which CSS removes in strings: `</s\<LF>tyle`

Comments are not a problem anymore: since https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20690, `isValidArbitrary` rejects every `/*` outside a string or an unquoted `url(…)`. So two values like `[--x:a()<//*)*/]` and `[--y:*/style>]` can't join into `</style` when the minifier removes the comment.

Other `</` text, like `content-['</>']`, still works. `@apply` of a discarded class gives the normal "Cannot apply unknown utility class" error.

## Test plan

- New tests in `candidate.test.ts` for the forms above, the escaped forms, escaped newlines, a comment that hides `</style`, and candidates with `<` that are still valid.
- I ran the bypass candidates through `compile()` and `optimize(css, { minify: true })`. None of them gives `</style` in the minified output.
- Fuzz runs (random candidate sets with `<`, `/`, `*`, comments, escapes, quotes and `url(…)` pieces) find no `</style` in the raw or the minified CSS.
- `pnpm run build` and all vitest projects pass.

Issues.Title: @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi 4.3.4 dropped "cpu": ["wasm32"], so npm installs the WASI fallback on every platform
Issues.Body:
# Draft upstream issue for tailwindlabs/tailwindcss

Title: `@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi 4.3.4 dropped "cpu": ["wasm32"], so npm installs the WASI fallback on every platform`

## What changed

`@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi` 4.3.3 declares `"cpu": ["wasm32"]` in its package.json. 4.3.4 and 4.3.5 declare no `cpu` field. Its `engines.node` also changed from `>=14.0.0` to `^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=23.5.0`.

## Reproduction (npm 11.19.1, Node 24.22.2, Linux x64)

```
npm view @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi@4.3.3 cpu --json   # ["wasm32"]
npm view @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi@4.3.4 cpu --json   # (empty: no cpu field)
npm view @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi@4.3.5 cpu --json   # (empty: no cpu field)
```

Install effect, with a project on `tailwindcss` + `@tailwindcss/vite` 4.3.3:

1. `npm ls @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi` is empty. `node_modules/@tailwindcss` contains `node`, `oxide`, `oxide-linux-x64-gnu` and `vite`. The lockfile entry for the wasm package has `"cpu": ["wasm32"]`, so npm skips it on x64.
2. `npm install tailwindcss@4.3.4 @tailwindcss/vite@4.3.4` (a patch bump). `node_modules/@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi` is now installed (about 6.7 MB on disk, 115 files). The lockfile gains six `inBundle` entries under it: `@emnapi/core`, `@emnapi/runtime`, `@emnapi/wasi-threads`, `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime`, `@tybys/wasm-util` and `tslib`. The wasm package's own lockfile entry no longer has `"cpu"`.

(4.3.5 was not installed; its registry metadata matches 4.3.4.)

## Expected

A patch release does not change which platforms install the WASI fallback. Either the package keeps `"cpu": ["wasm32"]`, as in 4.3.3, or the change is intentional and documented, for example in the changelog.

## Actual

Every platform, including Linux, macOS and Windows CI runners and Vercel builds, installs about 6.7 MB of WASI fallback plus six bundled packages that nothing loads. `@tailwindcss/oxide/index.js` still prefers the native binding and only falls back to WASI when native loading fails or `NAPI_RS_FORCE_WASI` is set, so there is no functional break, only install size and lockfile churn.

## Impact

The lockfile diff for a patch bump grows by six packages and install size grows on every platform. We are holding `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/vite` at 4.3.3 until the restriction is restored or we decide to accept the fallback.

Is dropping `cpu` intentional (for example, so the fallback can be installed with `--cpu=wasm32` or on unsupported platforms)? If so, a note in the release notes would help. If not, please restore the field.

Issues.Title: Add a single-threaded browser build of `@tailwindcss/oxide`
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi` only has a threaded `wasm32-wasip1-threads` build. In browsers it needs `SharedArrayBuffer`, which is only available on cross-origin isolated pages (COOP/COEP headers), so the scanner can't run on most pages.

This adds a separate single-threaded `wasm32-wasip1` build for browsers:

- `browser.mjs` loads it with non-shared memory and scans an in-memory filesystem (memfs), exported as `__fs` and `__volume`. Scanning runs on the calling thread.
- The pinned NAPI CLI only builds `wasm32-wasip1-threads`, so `scripts/build-browser.mjs` builds the module with Cargo directly, and `build.rs` links emnapi's single-threaded archive. The script reads the artifact path from Cargo's JSON output, and fails the build when the module doesn't link against the memory that `browser.mjs` creates.
- The `browser` field of `@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi` now points to `browser.mjs`, and the package ships types (`index.d.ts`, `browser.d.mts`). The threaded browser loader (`tailwindcss-oxide.wasi-browser.js`, `wasi-worker-browser.mjs`) is still published, so code that imports it by path, for example on cross-origin isolated pages, keeps working.
- `@tailwindcss/oxide` gets a `browser` entry that re-exports the browser build.
- `build` now runs `build:browser`, so CI, the release workflows and CONTRIBUTING.md install the `wasm32-wasip1` target.

The Node.js and native builds are unchanged.

### Related

- Addresses the browser part of #11610: using Oxide on play.tailwindcss.com, and the `SharedArrayBuffer` errors when loading `@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi` in a browser. The edge runtimes from the original question (e.g. Deno Deploy) are not tested.
- An alternative to #18292, which builds `crates/oxide` for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with wasm-bindgen. This PR does not change the scanner code, because Rayon runs on the calling thread on `wasm32-wasip1`. It exposes the same `Scanner` API as Node.js instead of separate `Wasm*` types, and supports `scan()` over memfs. A `wasm32-unknown-unknown` build without the WASI runtime may be smaller.

## Test plan

- `pnpm --filter @tailwindcss/oxide test:ui`: new Playwright tests (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) serve the bundled entry without COOP/COEP headers. They check candidate extraction, UTF-16 positions, memfs discovery with incremental rescans, and use from an application-owned worker. One test makes `Worker` throw, to check that the build never creates workers.
- `pnpm test:integrations ./integrations/oxide/wasm.test.ts`: a new test loads the browser entry of the packed package in Node.js with `SharedArrayBuffer` removed.
- `pnpm --filter @tailwindcss/oxide build:browser`, with the default target directory and with `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR` set to another directory. Both copy the fresh module.
- Linked the module against memory that is too small, and against shared memory, to check that the build rejects both.
- `cargo check --target wasm32-wasip1 -p tailwind-oxide` works without `EMNAPI_LINK_DIR`.

Issues.Title: bun-plugin-tailwind: Windows drive-qualified CSS asset paths become ../../…/C:/… and fail to resolve
Issues.Body:
### What happens

On Windows, a relative `url()` in an imported CSS file is rebased with POSIX path rules, so a drive-qualified source path is treated as a relative path and the emitted URL climbs out of the drive:

```css
background-image:url("../../../../../../../H:/…/images/probe.svg")
```

Bun then fails the build because that relative URL does not exist.

### Versions

- `bun-plugin-tailwind` 0.1.2 (`packages/@tailwindcss-bun`), `tailwindcss` 4.3.3
- Bun 1.4.3 (`c6da4a4d3010e5553438c60f6bd76d981976867c`) and Bun 1.4.4 (`38afee6c84fcf48c0edb2466aa4b27d287a59c30`)
- Windows 11 10.0.26200 x64

### Minimal repro

Fixtures:

```css
/* app.css */
.card{background-image:url("./images/probe.svg")}
```

`images/probe.svg` is any SVG next to it.

Build a composed stylesheet in a staging directory (the shape a host build uses: host Tailwind CSS, `@source`, then the plugin's stylesheet), and run it through `Bun.build` with the plugin:

```ts
const styleEntry = "C:/tmp/staging/style.css";
await Bun.write(styleEntry, [
  `@import "C:/…/node_modules/tailwindcss/index.css";`,
  `@source "C:/tmp/fixture";`,
  `@import "C:/tmp/fixture/app.css";`,
].join("\n"));

const { default: tailwind } = await import("bun-plugin-tailwind");
const result = await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: [styleEntry],
  outdir: "C:/tmp/out",
  root: "C:/tmp/fixture",
  target: "browser",
  minify: true,
  plugins: [tailwind],
});
```

Actual: the build fails with

```
error: Could not resolve: "../../../../../../../H:/…/images/probe.svg"
    at C:/Users/…/AppData/Local/Temp/ulak-tw-repro-…/style.css:170:21
```

Expected: the asset resolves (an absolute path, a rebased relative path, or a data URL), with no `H:` segment inside a relative URL.

### Cause, as far as we can see

The URL is rebased relative to the composed stylesheet with `path.posix.relative`. Given a Windows source path (`H:/…/images/probe.svg`) and a different drive-qualified importer, `path.posix.relative` returns `../../…/H:/…/images/probe.svg`: the drive letter is treated as a normal segment. Using `path.win32.relative` on win32, or converting both sides through `file:` URLs and back to a URL path, would keep the drive out of a relative URL.

### Workaround we carry

At the composed-stylesheet resolver we match `^(?:\.\.\/)+[a-zA-Z]:\//` on `onResolve` and return the drive-qualified path embedded in it, which makes the build succeed. It is a workaround for every plugin build on Windows; a fix in the plugin would let us delete it.

### Impact

Every Windows build of a stylesheet that references a relative asset from an imported CSS file fails (or, without a resolver workaround, publishes a URL that 404s). The same stylesheet builds correctly on macOS and Linux.

Issues.Title: fix(oxide): relax engines.node to >= 10 for @tailwindcss/oxide
Issues.Body:
## Summary

### What
Relaxes `engines.node` from `>= 20` to `>= 10` for `@tailwindcss/oxide` and all 12 native platform packages (`crates/node/package.json` + `crates/node/npm/*/`). Adds changelog fragment `.changelog/oxide-engines-node.md`.

### Why
`@tailwindcss/oxide` ships prebuilt N-API binaries compiled against **N-API 3**, which is stable since Node.js 10.0.0. The `>= 20` constraint was introduced in `c6f0c6b3` as part of the Node 20 build-toolchain bump; it reflects build-time requirements, not runtime compatibility. It unnecessarily blocks `npm install` on Node 14/16/18 LTS environments that fully support N-API 3, forcing upgrades for CI pipelines, Docker images, and legacy systems.

### How
- Set `"engines": { "node": ">= 10" }` in:
  - `crates/node/package.json` (main package)
  - All 12 native platform packages under `crates/node/npm/` (android-arm-eabi, android-arm64, darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, freebsd-x64, linux-arm-gnueabihf, linux-arm64-gnu, linux-arm64-musl, linux-x64-gnu, linux-x64-musl, win32-arm64-msvc, win32-x64-msvc)

**Changelog fragment:** `.changelog/oxide-engines-node.md`
